headline: Trump says FBI is probing Huang case; Nvidia gets sued
dek: Shareholders accuse the company of misleading statements, per The Guardian.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Trump on the FBI
body: Trump said the FBI is looking into the case of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, per The Guardian and CNBC.
He defended Huang and said he thinks "he'll be in good shape" (The Guardian).

points.t: False or misleading statements about risks.
Said the meetings were not unusual (The Guardian).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Shares under pressure
body: Nvidia shares fell 4.3% on Monday, about $190 billion, per The Guardian.
On Tuesday they fell another 5.53%, according to CNBC.

stat.cap: of value lost in a day, says The Guardian

items.t: The earnings call is on Nov. 17 (SiliconANGLE).

caption.hook: Trump said the FBI is investigating Jensen Huang, and shareholders sued Nvidia.
body: Per The Guardian and CNBC, the U.S. president defended Nvidia's CEO at the White House and said he should be in good shape. On the same Monday, shareholders filed a class action in federal court in California, alleging false or misleading statements about the risks tied to the case.

The company's shares fell 4.3% on Monday, a loss of about $190 billion, and another 5.53% on Tuesday, per The Guardian and CNBC. SiliconANGLE notes that Nvidia reports earnings on Nov. 17, when Huang is likely to face questions about the case.
caption.cta: Will the lawsuit change how you see Nvidia?
